items.section: 3.6 Genetic sharing — a code and its machinery
items.text: Thirteen runs through the eukaryotic vault's counts and is absent from a prokaryotic homolog's. A human brain vault at 3.1 Å whole and 3.6 Å at the cap has 39 chains per half, 78 in the shell, 39-fold dihedral symmetry at the barrel and 13-fold symmetry at the cap, with two of every three monomers excluded in sequence from the pore. A rabbit liver vault at 2.3 Å whole and 2.25 Å at the cap has 39 chains per half, 39-fold dihedral symmetry through residue 803, and 13-fold symmetry at the cap, 13 copies of an asymmetric homotrimer from residue 804. A rat vault by X-ray at 3.5 Å has 39 copies per half and 78 in the shell. 39 = 3 x 13 and 78 = 6 x 13. The two cap counts arise at two species by two preparations and two reconstructions. A phage homolog at 3.2 Å carries no 13: 48 chains per half, 96 in the shell, 48-fold at the barrel, 16-fold at the cap and 8-fold at the tip, with 48 = 16 x 3 and 96 = 2 x 48. A 9 A account of a rat vault instead reports 96 copies, 48 per half, phased with 48-fold symmetry, and parts from the 39-fold accounts; both stand. A further human account at 3.09 Å reports no cap symmetry mismatch. These are counts of chains and of rotational repeats at reconstructions, each at its own species, preparation and imposed symmetry.

items.sentence: Seating of genetic code on a prime ladder (protein-fold with 13, organism-fold with 37, numbers along seventeen primes) is reading, not cohering — a possibling.
